target_audience_note: "Complete protection independent from statutory health insurance." — the document states no customer category.
summary: Insurance Product Information Document issued by DKV Luxembourg S.A. for the COMPLETE HEALTH tariff, a Private Health Insurance described as complete protection independent from statutory health insurance. Cover concerns outpatient treatment, dental treatment and inpatient treatment, plus the BEST CARE + / BEST CARE PREMIUM + tariff services, and applies to Europe. The document states that the scope of insurance also includes the free of charge protection according to the TRAVEL + tariff; the corresponding TRAVEL / TRAVEL + information sheet is bound into the same PDF on pages 3-4.

duration_and_cancellation.duration: Insurance cover commences in accordance with the time period stated in the policy document (commencement of insurance); however, not before the insurance contract has been concluded, i.e. not before the insurance policy has been signed by both contractual partners and not before the termination of waiting periods. Insurance cover ends – including any insurance claims which may be still pending – when the insurance contract is terminated. For TRAVEL / TRAVEL + (p. 4): The beginning and the end of the insurance cover are indicated in the General Terms and Conditions.
duration_and_cancellation.notice_period: Period of notice to cancel the insurance contract is 30 days.
methods: Cancellation must be effected in writing.
special_rights: The policyholder can contest the automatic renewal of the insurance contract by notifying the insurance company with effect at the end of the insurance year, however, not before termination of the second insurance year at the earliest.
As a policyholder, you may limit the cancelation of the insurance to a single insured person in your insurance contract.
The cancellation is only valid provided that the policyholder can prove that the insured persons affected by this were informed of notification to cancel.
In some situations, you might have an extraordinary cancellation right, e.g. if premium contributions are subject to an increase.

Insurance cover is terminated, for example; in case of: Cancellation of the insurance contract; Death of the insured person; Non-compliance with the requirements of a risk/person to be insured stipulated in the tariff conditions.
TRAVEL / TRAVEL + (p. 4): The insurance contract ends automatically with the termination date indicated on the policy. There is no automatic renewal of the insurance contract.

notes: The first instalment/premium payment must be paid at the latest immediately after the insurance policy has been given to the policy holder, however, not before the inception date of insurance cover indicated on the insurance policy.
All other premiums are due, depending on the agreed method of payment, at the beginning of the agreed contribution period.

Premium payment can be effected via bank transfer or via direct debit mandate in favor of the insurer. Should you opt for monthly instalments, it is indispensable to arrange for a direct debit mandate in favor of the insurer.
In some situations, you might have an extraordinary cancellation right, e.g. if premium contributions are subject to an increase.
TRAVEL / TRAVEL + (p. 4): Premium payment has to be effected immediately.
TRAVEL / TRAVEL + (p. 4): Premium payment can be effected via credit card or Digicash.

gaps: THIS PDF CONTAINS TWO DIFFERENT IPIDs, and the schema carries one product. Pages 1-2 are the IPID for 'DKV Luxembourg S.A.  -  Product : COMPLETE HEALTH'; pages 3-4 are a complete, self-standing IPID for 'DKV Luxembourg S.A.  -  Product : TRAVEL / TRAVEL +' — its own 'What type of insurance is it ?' ('Travel Insurance for journeys abroad'), its own covered / not-covered / restrictions boxes, its own obligations, payment, start-end and cancellation sections. product_name is COMPLETE HEALTH (the task metadata and the first sheet agree). The second sheet was NOT discarded: page 1 states that 'The scope of insurance also includes the free of charge protection according to the TRAVEL + tariff (see separate information sheet)', so its content belongs to what a COMPLETE HEALTH policyholder is covered for. Every item taken from it is prefixed 'TRAVEL / TRAVEL + (separate information sheet, p. 3) – ' and cites page 3 or 4, so a reader can always tell the two sheets apart. Note that branch is 'sante' from the task metadata while the second sheet is a travel product; both sheets are nevertheless badged 'Private Health Insurance' in their own footer line.

edition_date: null — neither sheet prints an edition/version date or a reference code. The whole text layer of all four pages was searched for date and version patterns: no hit. The PDF metadata carry a creation date (2019-12-12) and a modification date (2019-12-19); that is metadata, not print, and was NOT used as edition_date.

Polarity of the lists: the markers are BITMAP IMAGES, neither text nor vector drawings. Page 1: 32 image markers — 21 green ticks (7.16 × 7.94 pt, x0 = 29.8), 7 red crosses (7.16 × 7.22 pt, x0 = 307.4), 4 orange exclamation marks (2.39 × 8.87 pt, x0 = 309.4); 21 + 7 + 4 = 32. Page 3: 28 markers — 13 ticks, 12 crosses, 3 exclamation marks; 13 + 12 + 3 = 28. Page 2 and page 4: 2 ticks each ('Where am I covered ?'). Every count closes against the extracted items. Marker shape and colour were confirmed on a 6× render of a sibling document from the same template. These facts cannot appear in key_quotes: they are not in the text layer.

One item on page 1 is printed WITHOUT a marker and was kept: 'The scope of insurance also includes the free of charge protection according to the TRAVEL + tariff (see separate information sheet)'. It sits below the last BEST CARE tick, inside the 'What is insured ?' box, and it is the sentence that ties the two sheets together — dropping it to make the tick count match the item count would have hidden the link. Page 3 carries the same kind of unmarked line: 'The maximum amounts specified in the General Terms and Conditions of insurance apply to the benefits specified.', recorded as the limits of every TRAVEL item and in special_conditions.

Column-inversion check NEGATIVE on both sheets: the flat text emits each left column in full before its right column, with no interleaving, although the y-ranges overlap throughout (a tick at y = 369.5 and a cross at y = 369.5 on page 1). Attachment was rebuilt marker by marker on the abscissa rather than taken from reading order. Recorded because a negative control is only valid for the document it was run on.

The two sheets carry different item sets in identically-named boxes — for instance 'Medical aids such as hearing aids, arch supports' is covered on sheet 1, while sheet 2 covers 'Medical aids that become necessary for the first time during a stay abroad and as a consequence of an accident (excluding vision or hearing aids)'. They were kept strictly separate; nothing from one sheet was used to complete the other.
target_audience: null. Neither sheet names a customer category; the document's own wording is in target_audience_note. Not deduced from the product type.
The length of the waiting periods is never stated; waiting_periods.duration stays null. Sheet 2 mentions no waiting period at all.
Neither sheet states a deductible/franchise, a prescription period or a claims procedure; deductibles, prescription_period and claims_procedure stay empty.

No item on either sheet is presented as optional — unlike the sibling COMPACT HEALTH and HOSPITAL HEALTH sheets, the BEST CARE block here is headed 'Tariff BEST CARE + / BEST CARE PREMIUM +' with the condition '(in case of full insurance coverage for inpatient treatments)' rather than 'Optional service'. is_optional is therefore false throughout, and that condition is recorded in conditions[].
Spelling kept verbatim as printed, not corrected: 'Accomodation costs (including single room)' on sheet 1 against 'Accommodation costs' on sheet 2, and 'co-insured' on sheet 1.

Text-layer trap check: no zero-width spaces, no soft hyphens, no NFD combining accents, no PUA glyphs, no U+0007, no text outside the page rectangle, no stacked headers. One curly apostrophe (U+2019, in 'an insured person’s pregnancy') and 24 thin spaces U+2009 were found and preserved verbatim in the quotes rather than normalised.

The risk carrier is named on BOTH sheets: 'DKV Luxembourg S.A.' (page 1 and page 3 footers, with legal form). No third party (claims handler, assistance company, broker) is named anywhere in the document.
The PyMuPDF re-extraction performed here is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the text supplied in the prompt (10234 = 10234 characters); the text was not truncated.
